conventional.policy_description: Repeal the deduction for foreign-derived intangible income (FDII). Published estimate: raises about \$158B over ten years (Treasury, FY2025 Green Book, before the R&D proposal Treasury pairs it with).

credibility.no_band_reason: the one pre-registered corporate row is a statutory rate change, not a GILTI, FDII or Pillar Two reform
credibility.own_row_caption: Unfitted reconstruction, 29.9% from -$158B (U.S. Treasury) — no constant is fitted to this figure.
limitations: holdout labels follow the locked post-2026-05-02 regression protocol; they are not retroactive historical out-of-sample claims.
No pre-registered out-of-sample row scores a policy of this class, so this model's accuracy on one has not been measured.

Scored by one base x rate identity — FDII income x the deduction rate x the statutory rate — on an income implied by Treasury OTA's own tax expenditure for the deduction ($130,230M over FY2025-2034, Tax Expenditures FY2026 Table 1 line 5). The module therefore reproduces that published cost by construction and the whole of this row's error is the distance between it and the carried target.

The IRC 250(a)(3) step-down from a 37.5% to a 21.875% deduction in TY2026 is inside the published path the income base is inverted from, so the window average reflects it, but the module's scalar interface cannot say which years are which.

No behavioural relocation of intangible property, and no interaction with the GILTI rate change. Treasury's own gross repeal row is $157,993M, 21% above their tax expenditure, because Green Book proposals are scored on a baseline already carrying the same volume's 28% corporate rate.

Treasury pairs that row one-for-one with 'Provide additional support for research and development expenditures' and prints a subtotal of $0; the module scores repeal without the R&D offset, which is the gross row. Treasury scores it on a baseline that already carries the same volume's 28% corporate rate, which is where its ~21% premium over the $13.023B/yr tax expenditure the module inverts comes from.
credibility.caption: No out-of-sample band: the one pre-registered corporate row is a statutory rate change, not a GILTI, FDII or Pillar Two reform. The 44 pre-registered Tier 1 rows are the only tier that measures this model's accuracy, and none of them scores a policy of this kind.
